Propose how to implement a new read-only CLI flag `vajra next --list-roles` that prints every registered fleet role and its tool grant.

Context: This is the Vajra project (a Rust launcher/governance wrapper over coding agents). Recent sessions (S126) have been "finishing the fleet" — registering the last five SDLC agent roles. The fleet roles and their tool grants are defined/registered somewhere in the codebase. `vajra next` is an existing subcommand with several read-only flags (e.g. --plan, --check-plan, --design, --stations, --list-roles is NEW).

Your job (read-only advice only — do NOT write any code):
1. Locate where the `next` subcommand and its existing flags are parsed and dispatched (likely in src/), and where the fleet roles + their tool grants are registered/defined. Cite the real files and line numbers.
2. Propose the concrete shape of the `--list-roles` flag: where it plugs into the existing `next` arg parsing, what function it calls, and how it reads the registered roles + tool grants (reuse the existing registry, do not duplicate the role list).
3. Specify the output format (each registered role + its tool grant), keeping it consistent with how other `vajra next` read-only flags print.
4. Name the single test that would fail without this change (which test file, what it asserts), following the project's existing test conventions.
5. Keep it minimal and within the project's house patterns. Flag any footguns (e.g. a hardcoded role list that would drift from the registry).

Return a brief, concrete implementation brief with file:line citations. Do not implement anything.

572	            new_body.len(),

645	/// A handoff is well-formed iff it carries every frontmatter contract key, a non-empty findings
646	/// body, AND the `## Handoff Delta` section (DECISION-007). Used by the fail-closed governance: a
647	/// malformed or empty handoff must NEVER read as a successful step. `Err(reason)` names the first
648	/// missing piece.
649	pub fn validate_handoff(text: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
650	    for key in FRONTMATTER_KEYS {
651	        if !text.lines().any(|l| l.trim_start().starts_with(key)) {
652	            return Err(format!("handoff missing frontmatter key `{key}`"));
653	        }
654	    }
655	    if !text.contains("## Handoff Delta") {
656	        return Err("handoff missing `## Handoff Delta` section".into());
657	    }
658	    match handoff_body(text) {
659	        Some(b) if !b.trim().is_empty() => Ok(()),
660	        _ => Err("handoff has an empty findings body".into()),
661	    }
662	}

664	/// The findings body — the content between the closing frontmatter fence and the `## Handoff Delta`
665	/// section, minus heading lines. `None` when the frontmatter fence or the delta section is absent.
666	/// Public so the ingest can extract a PRIOR handoff's body to feed `compute_delta` on a re-run.
667	pub fn handoff_body(text: &str) -> Option<String> {
668	    let after_fm = text.strip_prefix("---\n")?;
669	    let close = after_fm.find("\n---\n")?;
670	    let rest = &after_fm[close + 5..];
671	    let (before_delta, _) = rest.split_once("## Handoff Delta")?;
672	    let body: Vec<&str> = before_delta
673	        .lines()
674	        .map(|l| l.trim())
675	        .filter(|l| !l.is_empty() && !l.starts_with('#'))
676	        .collect();
677	    Some(body.join("\n"))
678	}

680	/// sha256 of a byte string — the handoff's `source-sha` preimage (the subagent's raw findings), so
681	/// a governed handoff is verifiably derived from those exact findings. Shells out (same tool-fallback
682	/// order as `verify-closeout.sh#_sha256`) rather than add a crate for one hash; this codebase already
683	/// shells to git/sha tools throughout.
684	pub fn sha256_hex(bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<String> {
685	    let variants: [(&str, &[&str]); 2] = [("sha256sum", &[]), ("shasum", &["-a", "256"])];
686	    for (cmd, args) in variants {
687	        let mut child = match Command::new(cmd)
688	            .args(args)
689	            .stdin(Stdio::piped())
690	            .stdout(Stdio::piped())
691	            .stderr(Stdio::null())
692	            .spawn()
693	        {
694	            Ok(c) => c,
695	            Err(_) => continue,
696	        };
697	        if let Some(mut stdin) = child.stdin.take() {
698	            if stdin.write_all(bytes).is_err() {
699	                continue;
700	            }
701	        }
702	        if let Ok(out) = child.wait_with_output() {
703	            if out.status.success() {
704	                if let Some(h) = String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stdout)
705	                    .split_whitespace()
706	                    .next()
707	                {
708	                    return Some(h.to_string());
709	                }
710	            }
711	        }
712	    }
713	    None
714	}

769	/// The three honest outcomes of looking for a role's handoff. `Absent` is the silent, harmless
770	/// case (most sessions have no researcher handoff and must behave exactly as before). `Malformed`
771	/// is deliberately NOT silent: a file that exists but fails the contract is a problem to surface,
772	/// not to swallow.
773	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
774	pub enum HandoffRead {
775	    /// No handoff file for this role/session.
776	    Absent,
777	    /// A file exists but does not satisfy the DECISION-007 contract. Carries (path, reason).

783	/// Parse handoff TEXT into a `Handoff` (pure — the testable core). `session`/`path` come from where
784	/// it was found rather than from the frontmatter: the path is the placement SoT, and trusting a
785	/// self-declared `session:` would let a misfiled handoff claim any session it liked.
786	pub fn parse_handoff(text: &str, session: u32, path: &str) -> Result<Handoff, String> {
787	    validate_handoff(text)?;
788	    let body = handoff_body(text).ok_or_else(|| "handoff has no findings body".to_string())?;
789	    // Every displayed field must come from the FRONTMATTER BLOCK, not merely from somewhere in the
790	    // file. `validate_handoff` accepts a `role:` line anywhere (it scans all lines), so without this
791	    // a file whose keys sit in the body would parse into a `Handoff` with blank fields and render as
792	    // "  (agent: , captured: )" — a broken artifact reading as a good one. Fail closed instead.
793	    let field = |key: &str| {
794	        frontmatter_value(text, key)
795	            .ok_or_else(|| format!("handoff frontmatter block has no `{key}` value"))
796	    };
797	    Ok(Handoff {
798	        role: field("role:")?,
799	        session,
800	        path: path.to_string(),
801	        agent: field("agent:")?,
802	        captured: field("captured:")?,
803	        source_sha: field("source-sha:")?,
804	        body,
805	    })
806	}

808	/// The value of a frontmatter `key:` line, trimmed. Only the frontmatter block is searched (the
809	/// text before the closing `---` fence), so a body line that merely starts with `agent:` cannot
810	/// impersonate a frontmatter field.
811	fn frontmatter_value(text: &str, key: &str) -> Option<String> {
812	    let after_fm = text.strip_prefix("---\n")?;
813	    let close = after_fm.find("\n---\n")?;
814	    after_fm[..close]
815	        .lines()
816	        .find_map(|l| l.trim_start().strip_prefix(key))
817	        .map(|v| v.trim().to_string())
818	        .filter(|v| !v.is_empty())
819	}

821	/// Read one role's governed handoff for `session` back off disk (the module's one narrow read
822	/// edge — fs-read-only, no writes, no processes; testable against a tempdir). An unreadable file
823	/// is reported as `Malformed`, never silently `Absent`.
824	pub fn read_handoff(root: &std::path::Path, role: &Role, session: u32) -> HandoffRead {
825	    let rel = role.handoff_rel(session);
826	    let path = root.join(&rel);
827	    if !path.exists() {
828	        return HandoffRead::Absent;
829	    }
830	    match std::fs::read_to_string(&path) {
831	        Err(e) => HandoffRead::Malformed(rel, format!("unreadable: {e}")),
832	        Ok(text) => match parse_handoff(&text, session, &rel) {
833	            Ok(h) => HandoffRead::Found(h),
834	            Err(reason) => HandoffRead::Malformed(rel, reason),
835	        },
836	    }
837	}

840	/// session simply had no fleet work, which every caller must treat as normal and silent.
841	pub fn read_handoffs(root: &std::path::Path, session: u32) -> Vec<HandoffRead> {
842	    ROLES
843	        .iter()
844	        .map(|r| read_handoff(root, r, session))
845	        .filter(|h| !matches!(h, HandoffRead::Absent))

847	}

849	/// Render read handoffs as the block a consuming station prints: who produced it, when, where it
850	/// lives, and the first `head` findings lines INLINE (a path alone is not consumption). Empty
851	/// input renders the empty string — absence prints nothing at all.
852	pub fn format_handoff_brief(reads: &[HandoffRead], head: usize) -> String {
853	    let mut s = String::new();
854	    for r in reads {
855	        match r {
856	            HandoffRead::Absent => {}
857	            HandoffRead::Malformed(path, reason) => {
858	                s.push_str(&format!(
859	                    "  ⚠ {path} exists but does not satisfy the handoff contract ({reason}) \
860	                     — not used\n"
861	                ));
862	            }
863	            HandoffRead::Found(h) => {
864	                s.push_str(&format!(
865	                    "  {role} (agent: {agent}, captured: {captured})\n    {path}\n",
866	                    role = h.role,
867	                    agent = h.agent,
868	                    captured = h.captured,
869	                    path = h.path,
870	                ));
871	                for line in h.head_lines(head) {
872	                    let clipped: String = line.chars().take(110).collect();
873	                    let ell = if line.chars().count() > 110 {
874	                        "…"
875	                    } else {
876	                        ""
877	                    };
878	                    s.push_str(&format!("    · {clipped}{ell}\n"));
879	                }
880	                // Never let a truncated head read as the whole brief — say how much was left out
881	                // and where the rest is. A partial view that looks complete is a false green.
882	                let omitted = h.omitted_lines(head);
883	                if omitted > 0 {
884	                    s.push_str(&format!(
885	                        "    · … {omitted} more line(s) — full findings at {}\n",
886	                        h.path
887	                    ));
888	                }
889	            }
890	        }
891	    }
892	    s
893	}

753	/// Whether the founder pre-authorized commits for THIS session at launch (S99).
754	///
755	/// The S97 Ladder-Rung-1 blocker (b): `commit.autonomous: false` + `require_user_approval: true`
756	/// are satisfiable only by a conversational approval token, and a headless `-p` run has no channel
757	/// to receive one — so an unattended session can never commit, and the Coder station can never
758	/// record a sha. The token has an out-of-band form already (`VAJRA_ALLOW_COMMIT=NN`, the S93
759	/// un-forgeable env marker the L3 guard enforces); what was missing is that nothing TELLS the
760	/// agent it exists. This classification mirrors `scripts/hook-commit-guard.sh` exactly so the
761	/// packet can never say "pre-granted" where the guard would block.
762	///
763	/// **Honest bound (disclosed):** this reads `vajra next`'s own process environment, which the
764	/// agent controls — so the line is ADVISORY, never a permission. The un-forgeable teeth stay with
765	/// the L3 guard, which reads its OWN launch env before the command runs; an agent that inlines
766	/// the marker gets an explicit BLOCK there regardless of what this line said.
767	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
768	enum CommitAuth {
769	    /// Marker present and valid for this session — the guard would ALLOW.
770	    PreGranted(String),
771	    /// Marker present but scoped to a different session — the guard would BLOCK.
772	    Mismatch { marker: String, session: String },
773	    /// No marker — a human approval token in chat is the only route.
774	    TokenRequired,
775	}
776	
777	/// Classify the launch environment against the branch-derived session, exactly as the L3 guard
778	/// does: session digits come from a `session-NN-*` branch; off such a branch the guard accepts any
779	/// non-empty marker, so the packet reports the same.
780	fn commit_authorization(branch: &str, marker: Option<&str>) -> CommitAuth {
781	    let session = branch
782	        .strip_prefix("session-")
783	        .and_then(|rest| rest.split_once('-'))
784	        .map(|(digits, _)| digits)
785	        .filter(|d| !d.is_empty() && d.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()));
786	    match (marker.filter(|m| !m.is_empty()), session) {
787	        (None, _) => CommitAuth::TokenRequired,
788	        (Some(m), None) => CommitAuth::PreGranted(m.to_string()),
789	        (Some(m), Some(s)) if m == s => CommitAuth::PreGranted(m.to_string()),
790	        (Some(m), Some(s)) => CommitAuth::Mismatch {
791	            marker: m.to_string(),
792	            session: s.to_string(),
793	        },
794	    }
795	}

803	             guard remains the enforcing check."
